findings.summary: R69 now uses the canonical non-withdrawn dual-pool paper arXiv:2604.08075 with exact primary-source metadata and results. Withdrawn duplicate 2604.09613 is excluded once as X22 and does not inflate the retained corpus or prior-art count.
Every retained or rejected work has one reproducible final disposition. SeqRoute is retained only as R68; no contradictory or duplicate screening identity remains.

The refreshed primary sources invalidate algorithmic and integration priority: QUARTZ covers conditional cost quantiles and admission; MESS+/SLARouter cover online cost/SLA routing; MTRouter/SeqRoute cover global or session budgets; R2-Router covers joint model/output budget; Solo.io and Keel cover reserve-before-dispatch and outstanding monetary envelopes.
The approved boundary is an absence-of-found-evidence statement for a comparative monetary-liability/fault-semantics study, not proof of priority, algorithmic novelty, or systems-integration novelty.
S29 and S30 are two expanded/citation-chasing searches after material pass S28; both record no material new work through 2026-07-13 and the repaired screening identities are reproducible.

six_novelty_gate_answers.1_exact_new_element: No individual algorithmic or integration element is established as new. The only defensible candidate contribution is the evaluated formulation that distinguishes request under-reservation, prespecified fixed-cohort liability exceedance, selected outstanding-set exceedance, and tenant-window overshoot for priced output-token liabilities under delayed, duplicate, missing, late, and reordered settlement. The retained sources were not found to report that exact metric/fault evaluation; this is not proof of priority and permits no first claim.
six_novelty_gate_answers.2_known_individual_elements: Cost-quality routing, budget-constrained and online routing, sparse/selected-only feedback, virtual-queue SLA control, joint model/output-budget selection, global/session budget state, length and cost prediction, conditional quantiles, conformal risk control, drift adaptation, multi-tenant fairness, escrow and transactional recovery, hard governance filtering, reserve-before-dispatch, outstanding budget envelopes, provider-usage reconciliation, hierarchical isolation, PostgreSQL accounting, price versioning, periods, and approval workflows are all known individually.
six_novelty_gate_answers.3_closest_prior_work: R55 Solo.io is the closest public reserve-settle gateway; R62 QUARTZ is the closest peer-reviewed conditional-quantile admission system; R56 Keel is the closest documented monetary outstanding-liability envelope; R01 Token Budgets is the closest adaptive reservation/concurrency research preprint. R63/R71 are the closest online cost/SLA routers, R61/R68 the closest global/session-budget routers, R52/R06/R07 the closest calibrated routing-risk work, R03/R66 the closest length/cost routing work, and R45/R46/R49 the relevant transaction machinery.
six_novelty_gate_answers.4_more_than_systems_integration: No. The current boundary is not more than systems integration as an algorithmic contribution. It becomes scientifically defensible only as a preregistered comparative measurement and formal problem study with explicit event-specific probability statements, leakage-controlled selected feedback, strong practical and academic comparators, and reproducible negative/null results. The gateway/operator is the experimental vehicle, not a novelty claim.
six_novelty_gate_answers.5_falsifying_experiment: The claimed advantage is falsified if, at matched empirical overshoot risk and on identical streams, a Solo.io/Keel-style atomic fixed-estimate envelope, a Token-Budgets-style locked adaptive estimator, QUARTZ-style monetary quantile admission, or an adaptive-quantile plus cheapest-governance-compliant router matches GOV-AR on utilization, served quality, refusal, isolation, and faulty-event outcomes. It is also falsified if removing risk allocation does not move the frontier or if missing/late/duplicate events do not distinguish conservative liability semantics.
six_novelty_gate_answers.6_claim_to_remove_or_narrow: Remove every first-of-kind claim for cost-aware, budgeted, online, adaptive, conformal, quantile-aware, SLA, sparse-feedback, global-budget, joint model/token-budget, multi-tenant, reserve-settle, budget-envelope, idempotent-ledger, or gateway-governance functionality. Remove algorithmic risk-allocation novelty. Do not call nonzero-risk mode deterministic hard-budget enforcement. State only an assumption-scoped fixed-cohort probability bound and empirically measured risk-utilization/fault behavior if frozen evidence supports them.

approved_contributions: An assumption-scoped problem and safety formulation separating settled spend, unresolved estimated-cost liability, request under-reservation, fixed-cohort exceedance, selected-outstanding-set exceedance, and tenant-window overshoot.

A preregistered comparative measurement of risk-utilization, tenant isolation, drift, faulty-event behavior, and local overhead against practical envelopes, quantile admission, adaptive estimators, strict reservation, and strong routing baselines.
